title: Restored clearance of senescent neutrophils by tissue-resident macrophages limits organ aging.
data_url: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE319489 (single-cell RNA-seq); https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.0vt4b8hck (figure source data + code, CC0)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) processed files: cell_metadata.csv.gz has exactly 126,443 rows and 3 columns (barcode, sample, group), 8 samples, 4 groups (Agedflox 35,734 / Youngflox 34,671 / Agedwt 28,300 / Youngwt 27,738 cells), zero duplicate barcodes, zero missing values; features.tsv.gz has 27,398 gene symbols; a ranged read of the matrix header confirms 27,398 genes x 126,443 cells with 268,332,917 non-zero entries (file is 805 MB gzipped, so not fully downloaded). A cross-tabulation of barcode suffix against sample showed each mouse occupies its own 10x Genomics lane (suffix 1-8, one per sample, no overlap). I also listed all 20 Dryad files with names, sizes and SHA-256 checksums (298 KB total: 16 Source_Data_Fig*.xlsx plus 3 R scripts and a README).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The paper itself is paywalled (not in PubMed Central or Europe PMC), so the biology, the flow-cytometry efferocytosis assays, the plasma proteomics and the human-tissue findings come from the abstract and the GEO series description only. The Dryad file *contents* could not be opened: every Dryad download endpoint returned HTTP 401/403 to the API and to a browser-style request, so I know the file names and sizes but not the rows inside the figure source tables. Cell-type labels (Kupffer cells, senescent neutrophils) are described in the GEO summary but are absent from the deposited metadata.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO processed files download without login (I opened the metadata and features files). Dryad record is public and CC0 but its download endpoints returned 401/403 to me; the 805 MB count matrix is over the 50 MB cap, so recorded by metadata only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only label column is 'group' (four age x genotype conditions), which is a property of the mouse, not of a cell. Every biologically interesting label in the paper - Kupffer cell identity, senescent neutrophil status, efferocytosis capacity - is absent from the deposited files and would have to be constructed by clustering and manual annotation.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present as a full sparse count matrix (27,398 genes x 126,443 cells, 268M non-zeros) with gene symbols; no identifier resolution needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Matrix Market header declares integer counts (raw unique-molecule counts per gene per cell); ages are stated in months in the GEO design (6-8 vs 23-25).

a5_enough_rows.note: 126,443 cells look like plenty, but the independent unit is the mouse: 8 mice, exactly 2 per experimental group (verified in the metadata). Cells from one mouse are pseudoreplicates, so the effective sample size for any age or genotype label is 8.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2-3 GB as a sparse count matrix (268M non-zeros) after streaming the 805 MB gzipped Matrix Market file; smaller if genes are subset
a6_fits_laptop.note: Feasible on 16 GB with chunked reading, though the decompressed text is roughly 5-6 GB and must never be loaded dense.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO design says 8 samples, n=2 mice per group across 4 conditions; the metadata file matches exactly (8 samples, 2 per group). Matrix dimensions match the metadata and features row counts.

a8_label_provenance.note: 'group' is a real experimental assignment, but the labels anyone would actually model here (senescence, efferocytosis state) would be computed from the same expression features via published gene signatures such as SenMayo or SenePy - that is leakage by construction, and scoring cells with an existing tool then training on those scores would just distil that tool.

existing_models.name: scAgeClock (single-cell transcriptome human aging clock, gated multi-head attention neural network, npj Aging 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported as a human single-cell age predictor; I retrieved the article listing but not its evaluation table, so I am not quoting a number.

existing_models.name: scMLEAge (statistical framework predicting the age of individual cells, applied to Tabula Muris Senis mouse atlas)
existing_models.score_and_split: Applied across mouse tissues including liver; specific metrics not retrieved.

existing_models.name: SCALE (single-cell aging-level estimator, applied to >20 mouse tissues in Tabula Muris Senis)
existing_models.score_and_split: Knowledge-based feature selection producing tissue-level aging scores; no held-out number retrieved.

existing_models.name: SenePy (cell-type-specific senescence signatures from single-cell transcriptomics, Nature Communications 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Signature-scoring method validated by enrichment of the SenMayo gene set across tissues; not a held-out classifier.

existing_models.name: DeepScence (deep-learning detection of senescent cells in single-cell and spatial data, Cell Genomics 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published as a senescence detector for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics; metrics not retrieved.

existing_models.name: SenMayo (125-gene senescence signature, Nature Communications 2022)
existing_models.score_and_split: A published gene list, not a trained model; validated by enrichment in aged human and mouse tissues.

backbone.name: Geneformer or scGPT (single-cell transcriptome foundation models with open weights)
backbone.hardware: Embedding 126,443 cells on a laptop CPU would take many hours but is possible; a GPU would be strongly preferred.
backbone.licence: Geneformer and scGPT weights are publicly downloadable; licences not checked because the project was rejected at Part A.

integration.partner_dataset: Tabula Muris Senis (mouse multi-organ ageing single-cell atlas, includes liver across several ages) and the Guilliams human liver cell atlas, which the paper's own R scripts already reanalyse
integration.join_key: gene symbol / Ensembl gene identifier for features; cell-type label for alignment
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a transcriptomic ageing clock trained on a large multi-mouse atlas report the EP2-deleted aged liver as younger than the wild-type aged liver, i.e. can an independent clock confirm a claimed rejuvenation intervention?

controls.positive_control: The clock or classifier must separate the 23-25 month wild-type mice from the 6-8 month wild-type mice, and Kupffer cell markers (Clec4f, Timd4) must mark the macrophage cluster.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the group labels across mice (not across cells) and confirm accuracy collapses to chance; also train on lane identity alone to show how much of the signal is batch.
controls.external_validation: Tabula Muris Senis liver, which is an independently generated mouse liver ageing dataset - but it would supply the training data, leaving this paper's 8 mice as only a tiny test set.

honest_claim_h3: With 8 mice, 2 per condition, and each mouse sequenced in its own 10x lane, any model trained here could only claim 'I can tell which of these eight libraries a cell came from', not 'I can detect ageing or the effect of EP2 deletion'.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a liver cell's gene-expression profile to predict whether the mouse was old or young and whether the EP2 receptor was deleted.
plain_idea.train_on: Raw gene counts for each of 126,443 liver cells (27,398 genes, 268 million non-zero entries, verified in the files) from 8 mice: 2 each of young wild-type, aged wild-type, young EP2-knockout and aged EP2-knockout.
plain_idea.predict: The four-way experimental group of the cell's donor mouse. The truth comes from the experimental design - the mouse's age in months and whether tamoxifen-induced deletion of the EP2 (PTGER2) prostaglandin receptor was performed in its macrophages.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Ageing-intervention labs would want an independent, unbiased read-out of whether a treatment makes old tissue look young; here the design is too small to give one, which is itself worth recording.

more_or_better_data.why: 126,443 cells from 8 mice is far smaller in independent units than Tabula Muris Senis, the multi-organ mouse atlas that scMLEAge and SCALE were built on; the only unique element is the EP2-knockout arm, which has 4 mice.

confidence_score.why: With 2 mice per condition there is no replicate structure to estimate biological noise; the only replication is cells within a mouse, which measures sequencing depth, not biology.

models_beatable.why: The senescence tools (SenMayo 2022, SenePy 2025) are signature-scoring rather than honestly held-out classifiers, so they are in principle improvable - but not from this dataset, which has no ground-truth senescence label.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model can be run as a baseline on a task this data defines, because the data defines no cell-level label; the condition that our model sees everything theirs sees plus more fails outright.

ml_idea: The project considered was a cell-level four-way classifier (young/aged x wild-type/EP2-knockout) on the liver single-cell data, or a frozen single-cell foundation-model embedding plus a linear head scored as an ageing clock, with the EP2-knockout mice as a rejuvenation test. Both die on the same fact: the label is a property of the mouse and there are 8 mice, each perfectly confounded with its own sequencing lane.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the verified matrix header (268,332,917 non-zeros: roughly 2.1 GB as 32-bit sparse values plus indices) and the 805 MB gzipped file size; nothing was timed because the project was rejected before any model was built.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the independent units: open cell_metadata.csv.gz and run a group-by on 'sample' and 'group'. It takes one minute and returns 8 mice, 2 per group - which is the whole answer.

verdict_reason: A5, A2 and A8 all fail. The 126,443 cells come from only 8 mice (2 per condition, verified in the deposited metadata), and each mouse is its own 10x Genomics lane, so experimental group is perfectly confounded with sequencing batch and no honest held-out split exists. The deposited metadata contains nothing but barcode, sample and group: no cell-type annotation, no senescence or efferocytosis measurement, so every label worth predicting would have to be constructed from the same expression values the model reads, and existing tools (SenMayo, SenePy, DeepScence, scMLEAge, SCALE) already occupy that space. The Dryad deposit is figure source data (298 KB of plot-level spreadsheets with a handful of mice per bar) plus three reanalysis scripts, which is excellent for reproducing the paper and useless as a training set.
